title: Number Games
text: “I’ll make you pay with your life for messing with the spirit. Learn the hard way what you’ve done!”
Hearing Ark’s furious shout, I couldn’t help but flinch!
Wait, what!? Not only did it feel like I was the one being scolded, but why was I reacting so strongly to this?
“Oh no!? Hey, Cat, calm down! I’ll get the info out of these guys! Save the killing for later!”
Ho-kun frantically tried to calm Ark down.
“What’s your reason for targeting the cat?”
“Huh? Why would I tell you guys? I’m going to put it to good use and become a being that surpasses even that goddess.”
“Ah… I see. So that’s what you were taught. In that case, it’s a countermeasure against the cat… How ridiculous. It’s far too shallow.”
Ho-kun nodded as if he understood.
“Oink! Oink oink!”
“Guaaaah!?”
Just by making a move to dodge the attack, the blade embedded in Filolial-sama’s neck is sinking deeper.
“Ugh… Ark, Ho. Filolial-sama is suffering.”

What should I do now? Normally, I’d order Ark to stay put, let my hatred for the reincarnated one and the pig grow, temporarily hand Ark over to them to ensure Filolial-sama’s safety, and then retrieve him—but I find myself thinking I mustn’t do that. Why is that, I wonder? Ark is a “God Hunter,” so he shouldn’t flinch at something like this. In fact, since he’s a God Hunter, shouldn’t he be able to resolve this in no time? Just then, I recalled Ark’s demeanor during our training sessions with Ren, as well as Ho-kun’s explanation. Apparently, Ark is strong against those who impersonate gods, but against anyone else… I believe the story was that he’s completely helpless.
“It’s Motoyasu-kun’s request, isn’t it? It’s okay, so calm down.”
Ark, who had been furious, turned to face me and smiled. That’s a bit of a relief. He isn’t angry at me. Still, my true feelings are that I really don’t want Ark to get angry. It’s truly baffling.

“As a token of mercy toward you lot, I’ll play a little game with numbers. This includes the penalty for what you’ve done that’s unjust to the world. Resist to your heart’s content and despair. Know that the sin of blaspheming a spirit is heavier than annihilation!”
With that, Ark unfurled wings of light on his back.
“I’m in too! Take this!”
The reincarnated person began casting Magic.
“Whoa.”

When Ho-kun snapped his fingers, some kind of magic was cast on me. Is this… the same magic that Father cast on us when we fought the Crimson Swine itself? It felt similar. I could clearly see that what the reincarnated person was firing at us was a power that looked like the magic Ho-kun had used.
“Akashic Break!”

The incantation was terrifyingly fast; I could tell it was in a magical language, but I couldn’t decipher it. It looked like countless characters burst forth from the surroundings and flew toward Ark. But the attack on Ark just passed right through him and came flying straight at me instead!?
Ark spread his hands slightly and traced a line with his fingers to the side, and the flying characters burst and vanished.
“What!? You’re telling me my magic was nullified!? But my magic and abilities can’t be stopped by something like that!”
That’s when Ho-kun let out a deep sigh.

“You guys… are you stupid? That type of Magic channels the power of a library run by an overprotective cat guardian, you know? It’s practically like telling the one lending you that power to go ahead and kill you.”
Oh? Is that so?
“Oink! Oink-oink-iiih!”
“Take this! Drifa Aqua Slash! And my finishing move—”
The pig and his minions finished their incantations and were about to unleash their Magic at Ho-kun.

“Oh my, oh my? Not the cat, but me? At a time like this? Ah, if you don’t want to die, you’d better not target me like that. It’s obvious at a glance that after dealing an instant death with on-demand Magic, you’re going to strip me of my abilities.”
Boom! Just as whatever the reincarnated person had fired was about to hit Ho-kun, it burst into flames and ended up charring the reincarnated person instead.

“Good thing it was a discretionary Magic spell. If it had been a passive one, I wouldn’t be standing here right now. And if it had included a modification effect, everything I’d ever been involved with would’ve burned to ashes, leaving not even a speck of dust behind.”
Magic flared up and vanished, too. At the same time, those who’d attacked Ark let out cries of shock.
“Gyaa, Gyaaaaaaa!? W-what the—! M-my abilities, my stats are burning up!? What the hell is going on! Hey!”
“My abilities… they’re gone!? They’re just keep dropping!? You’ve got to be kidding meeeee!”
“What a joke. After getting so cocky, this is what you look like? If this isn’t pathetic, then what is…”
The once-gentle Ark has turned incredibly irritable and is hurling words of contempt at the reincarnated ones.

“You rotten fools might say that blabbing about your abilities to your opponent is something only an idiot would do, but unlike that cat over there, I’m in a really good mood right now, so I’ll explain it to you. My flames ignited your ability and set it ablaze. What you did was about as foolish as trying to look at the sun through a telescope that isn’t properly protected.”
“The same goes for Magic—every attack against me ignites and bounces right back at the user, spreading the flames,” Ho-kun added with a sigh.

“The more abnormal your ability is, the more it burns—but at this rate, you’re going to burn everything to the ground. The fact that the person’s ability who targeted the cat vanished is a whole other story.”
“It’s like you’ve committed the folly of drilling a hole in the bottom of a bucket full of water. Why should I have to explain myself when you guys won’t just come clean?”
Ark’s retort was just like my Father’s—an eye for an eye, I suppose.
“Nonsense! That can’t be right! There’s no way my foresight could be wrong!”
Foresight? What’s that? Is that another one of those ‘abilities’? I suppose it’s a power bestowed by the Crimson Swine itself.

“You call seeing only the future that suits you and manipulating fate ‘foresight’… Since it’s been wrong, why don’t you question the ability itself? A true seer is tormented by seeing too many possibilities, and ends up hoping that the worst future they foresee won’t come true.”
“Oink! Oink oink!”
The pig is squealing while holding Filolial-sama hostage. Then, Ho-kun spread the tips of his wings like hands… and a candle appeared.

“You’ve been taking hostages and shouting arrogantly this whole time, so I’m going to do the same. If you step in any further, you’ll die, you know? This is a candle representing your lifespan, shown this way so you can see it clearly. If you blow it out, you’ll die—are you sure you want to do that?”
Ho-kun’s words reminded me of a story that compares a person’s lifespan to a candle. Could it be that *that* really is a candle representing his lifespan?
“It’s kind of like what your fellow reincarnated person was doing, isn’t it? Since you call him a ‘comrade,’ you’ve surely seen him use that power to kill someone, right?”
“Oinkkkk! Oink! Oink-hahahaha!”

The pig mocked Ho-kun, who had produced the candle. What an ugly pig! It’s not enough for him to take Filolial-sama hostage—mocking Ho-kun, who is Filolial-sama’s superior, is a crime worthy of a thousand deaths! Just as I was feeling my anger flare up inside…
“Oh, right.”
Ho-kun blew out the candle with a puff…
“Bub—”
As if a string had snapped, the pig holding Filolial-sama hostage collapsed.
“Ooogggghhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh!?”
“Y-youuuuuuu! What the hell are you doingoooooo!?”

“What do you mean? I just blew out the candle like you told me to. You guys… could you stop underestimating your opponents already? If you’re so full of yourself that you think your strength surpasses even the gods and that we’d fall for that, that’s just plain arrogant, isn’t it?”
Whoa! This is Ho-kun’s show! He’s so incredibly strong that all I can do is watch.
“Ho-kun, you’re amazing!”
“Motoyasu-kun’s booming cheers don’t make me happy at all… Plus, that cat, now filled with murderous intent, doesn’t look like it’s going to calm down… Hmm, this has turned into quite a hassle.”
